title: Operator escape-hatches and binary fallback playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines operator-level "escape-hatches" and a tested binary-fallback path for private Redwood deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for use during severe runtime degradations, kernel/driver regressions, model binary failures, or when the primary serving runtime must be forcibly degraded to a minimal, validated inference binary to preserve customer SLAs. The document covers decision criteria, prerequisites, step-by-step procedures, verification checks, communication templates, and a customer requirements crosswalk.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: Field operators, SREs, on-call platform engineers, and customer success engineers performing emergency remediation for private deployments.
- Scope: Applies to: private VPC deployments managed by Redwood control plane, hybrid customers with an operator on-site, and fully air-gapped on-prem clusters. Not intended for hosted Redwood instances.

Key goals
---------
1) Provide deterministic, low-risk procedures to:
   - Transition traffic to a minimal inference binary (safe-mode) when the primary runtime is unstable.
   - Revert to previously validated binary artifacts quickly (binary fallback).
   - Ensure telemetry and audit evidence are captured for post-incident analysis.
2) Define clear owner responsibilities and SLO gating to minimize customer impact.

When to use this playbook (trigger conditions)
----------------------------------------------
Use these escape-hatches only when one or more of the following are true:
1. Token-level error rate crossing: >= 5% client-facing error rate for > 3 minutes AND sustained latencies > 3x SLO (see SLOs below).
2. KV-cache corruption or severe state divergence where soft restarts repeatedly fail to clear errors.
3. Primary runtime introduces regressions after an upstream kernel/driver upgrade that cannot be resolved within the maintenance window.
4. Binary or model-loading path causes node-level GPU lockups impacting > 10% of pool.

SLOs and thresholds referenced in this playbook
----------------------------------------------
- Per-tenant p95 latency SLO: 200ms (interactive workloads); emergency fallback allowed if latency <= 800ms for degraded mode.
- Error budget guardrail for fallback: less than 2% fatal error rate post-fallback (we aim to restore to <=1%).
- Customer notification threshold: if fallback will affect more than 1 high-priority tenant or >10% of requests, notify CS and account owner within 15 minutes.

Prerequisites and pre-validated artifacts
----------------------------------------
- Validation matrix entry exists for the fallback binary (artifact tag, SHA-256) stored in the release bucket. Example: redwood-safe-infer:v2025.11-rc2 (sha256:abc...).
- A signed, pinned package for on-prem: redwood-safemode-image-2026.01.tar.gz with accompanying signature file and verified checksum.
- Runbook owner has access to customer-specific control-plane keys, KMS token rotation window, and the operator vault.
- Customer acceptance: check customer deployment conformance record (see related_pages) for compatibility flags (gpu-driver, kernel-version, cgrouplist).

Decision matrix (high level)
---------------------------
- If node-level GPU hangs are present and cannot be isolated within 10 minutes -> perform node-evac + safe-mode drain on affected nodes.
- If control-plane model-loading errors are widespread across zones and root cause points to recent runtime change -> initiate binary fallback on all replicas in canary then cohort roll.

Primary escape-hatches (ordered by risk)
----------------------------------------
1) Soft drain + rolling restart of agents (low risk).
2) Canary swap: deploy safe-mode binary to 1-2 replicas (medium risk) and validate telemetry for 10 minutes.
3) Full cohort binary fallback (higher risk): switch all replicas to safe-mode, disable advanced optimizations (quantization fallback), and serve using stateless mode when needed.
4) Network-level traffic-steering to an alternate provisioned Dedicated pool (highest operational cost) if available.

Operator runbook: Canary safe-mode swap (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------------
Preconditions: Canary target selected (prefer non-primary zone), artifact present, operator on-call and CS informed.
1. Announce intent: post in incident channel and notify CS: "Initiating safe-mode canary for tenant X in zone Y".
2. Verify artifact checksum: sha256sum redwood-safemode:v2026.01 -> compare with release manifest.
3. Create canary deployment:
   - For Kubernetes-based private deployments: 
     kubectl -n redwood apply -f safemode-canary-deployment.yaml
   - safemode-canary-deployment.yaml should reference the pinned image and set replicaCount: 2.
4. Update service selector to include canary pods with weight=10% (traffic-split). Example: Istio VirtualService weighted routing snippet.
5. Monitor for 10 minutes for: p50/p95 latencies, 5xx rate, error logs mentioning "model-load" or "gpu-fence". Use these dashboards: CONFLUENCE-DB-DASH-OPS (internal link).
6. Validation checks (all must PASS):
   - p95 latency <= 3x SLO baseline for canary
   - Fatal errors < 0.5% of canary requests
   - No new OOM or GPU driver resets on canary nodes
7. If checks PASS: escalate to cohort fallback plan. If FAIL: rollback canary and proceed to deeper investigation (see triage checklist).

Binary fallback: full cohort procedure
------------------------------------
The cohort fallback is intended when canary shows success or incident severity mandates a fast switch.
1. Freeze control-plane routing policies: set emergency flag to bypass advanced routing.
2. Take a rolling snapshot of runtime state (KV cache manifest) for potential rollback. Command: redwood-admin state snapshot --namespace tenant-123 --out /tmp/kv-snapshot-<ts>.json
3. Apply cohort deployment update using the pinned safemode image with immutable tags. For k8s: kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/serving redwood-serving=redwood-safemode:v2026.01 --record
4. Disable model hot-swap features via configmap: redwood-serving-config -> safe_mode: true, hot_swap: false, advanced_quant: disabled.
5. Progressively increase traffic weight to safemode across zones using traffic orchestration (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%), validating telemetry at each step (10 minutes).
6. Post-fallback verification checklist (all must PASS):
   - Total error-rate <= 2%
   - p95 latency within emergency latency target
   - No new hardware faults reported by GPU telematics
   - Customer-visible degradation logged and CS notified
7. If any critical check fails during increase, execute immediate rollback to snapshot and previous image using recorded kubectl rollout undo or image revert.

Rollback to previous binary (safest path)
----------------------------------------
- If cohort fallback failed, revert to snapshot+previous-image:
  1) kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/serving --to-revision=<prev_rev>
  2) Reapply configmap values for advanced features.
  3) Validate KV cache integrity against snapshot and mark suspect keys for eviction.

Escape-hatch commands (cheat-sheet)
----------------------------------
- Check node GPU resets: journalctl -u nvidia-gpu-manager | tail -n 200
- Evacuate a node safely: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- Create safemode canary: kubectl apply -f safemode-canary-deployment.yaml
- Promote image and record: kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/serving redwood-serving=redwood-safemode:v2026.01 --record
- Snapshot state: redwood-admin state snapshot --namespace <ns> --out /tmp/kv-<ts>.json
- Force rollback: kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/serving --to-revision=<rev>

Testing and validation playbook (pre-incident preparation)
--------------------------------------------------------
Operators must perform the following quarterly checklist:
1. Verify safemode artifacts exist and checksums match release manifest.
2. Run a simulated canary in a staging cluster: deploy safemode image, run 10k synthetic inference requests with the production prompt set, measure latencies and failure rates.
3. Test on-prem signing: ensure tarball signature verifies for at least two recent hardware/driver combinations declared in the customer requirements matrix.
4. Run the traffic-split automation and assert that rollback completes within 8 minutes when invoked.

Customer requirements crosswalk (minimum compatibility table)
----------------------------------------------------------
This table maps the minimum customer environment fields required for the escape-hatches to be viable.

| Requirement | Minimum / Acceptable values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel version | >= 5.15 (preferred) | Older kernels may lack required GPU driver features. |
| NVIDIA driver | 525.105+ | For stable CUDA 12 kernels; if lower, safemode disables some opt paths. |
| Container runtime | containerd 1.6+ or Docker 24+ | Must support immutable image tags and user namespace mapping. |
| K8s version | 1.24 - 1.27 supported | We maintain compatibility matrix in related_pages. |
| Entitlements | Operator account with cluster-admin or curated role | Required for node drain and rollout operations. |

Operational responsibilities and ownership
-----------------------------------------
- Incident commander: on-call platform lead (engineering) — coordinates canary and cohort decisions.
- Operator: SRE performing the kubectl/agent operations.
- Customer Success: responsible for customer notification templates and post-incident QBR.
- Security: audits any binary switching and confirms signatures/attestations.

Communication templates
-----------------------
Use the following minimal template for customer notification when initiating a cohort fallback: 

Subject: Planned emergency fallback for Redwood runtime affecting [TENANT]
Body: We are experiencing a runtime instability affecting inference traffic for [TENANT]. We will enact an emergency fallback to a validated safe-mode binary to restore availability. Expected impact: transient latency increase and temporary loss of advanced optimization features. Estimated ETA for full recovery: 60-120 minutes. We will provide updates every 15 minutes.

Post-incident checklist and evidence capture
------------------------------------------
1. Preserve snapshots and kube events: kubectl get events -n redwood --since=2h > /var/incident/events-<ts>.log
2. Export telemetry window covering 30 minutes pre-incident to 60 minutes post-fallback.
3. Attach signed artifact and checksum used for fallback to incident ticket.
4. Perform RCA and update the validation matrix with lessons learned and new kernel/driver combinations.

Appendix A: Sample safemode-canary-deployment.yaml (minimal)
-----------------------------------------------------------
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redwood-safemode-canary
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-serving
      cohort: safemode-canary
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: redwood-serving
        cohort: safemode-canary
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: redwood-serving
        image: registry.redwood.internal/redwood-safemode:v2026.01
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1

Appendix B: Related pages and artifacts
--------------------------------------
- Deployment conformance matrix: CONFLUENCE-DEP-CONF-2026 (related_pages)
- Release manifest (artifact store): s3://redwood-release/manifest/2026-01.json
- Incident evidence template: CONFLUENCE-INC-EVIDENCE-TEMPLATE

Notes and warnings
------------------
- Do not perform full cohort fallback unless canary validation has passed, unless the incident meets the severity triggers above.
- Always collect signed artifact checksums and timestamps prior to changing images; these are required for compliance for some enterprise customers.
- If the customer environment lacks the minimum kernel or driver version, fallbacks will reduce feature parity and may require a coordinated maintenance window.
